transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Jon Park (Redwood SE), Leila O'Connell (Redwood Solutions), Elias Novak (Halcyon CTO), Priya Menon (Halcyon Head of Security), Marco Ruiz (Halcyon Compliance), Sara Lin (Halcyon Platform)

Auto-generated sections (may be imperfect):
Topics: KMS options, data residency, region pinning, subprocessor list, audit logs, SOC2/ISO
Action items: see list

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Thompson: hey everyone thanks for joining, we uh we really appreciate the time. quick roll call?
[00:05] Elias Novak: hi this is elias, im the cto at halcyon, and i have priya, marco and sara on the call too.
[00:12] Priya Menon: hey all, priya here, security lead.
[00:15] Jon Park: jon from redwood, i'll drive the tech bits, hi all.
[00:20] Maya Thompson: great. agenda — high level: go through how we handle region pinning for EU vs US, options for KMS and key custody, what our subprocessor stack looks like, and logging / audit capabilities. then we can call out any compliance gaps. sound okay?
[00:33] Marco Ruiz: yes fine. primary ask: we need to ensure eu-resident customer data never leaves the eu for processing, unless we have explicit contractual basis. also want visibility into subprocessors.
[00:45] Leila O'Connell: quick note up front — we support three KMS patterns: 1) redwood-managed keys (default), 2) customer-managed keys (CMK) integrated with cloud KMS, and 3) split-key / escrow options for higher assurance. i'll explain each as we go.
[01:02] Sara Lin: can you clarify split-key? is that like split-hsm?
[01:05] Jon Park: yeah kind of — split in the sense of an escrow service where customer retains a part of key material or keys are held in a separate HSM that requires dual control to release for key rotation/escape hatch. it's not shipped to customers as a turnkey hsm, more of an operational pattern we can enable.
[01:22] Priya Menon: is your CMK integration full BYOK? meaning we can bring keys from our cloud provider and you never see plaintext?
[01:28] Jon Park: yes, for CMK we leverage standard KMS envelope encryption. Redwood never persists unencrypted model context with the plaintext key. we store only ciphertext and a key reference. with BYOK the key operations are proxied to your KMS. caveat: metrics and some telemetry require tokenization or partial PII redaction, but no raw payload access.
[01:45] Elias Novak: what about logs? i need detailed audit logs for access to keys and model inference requests that contain sensitive identifiers. retention policy needs to be 7 years for some EU customers due to regulator X.
[01:56] Maya Thompson: we can provide audit logs that show request id, model used, timestamp, region, and user token ID. for key operations we include kms-call traces — who asked, what operation, and whether it succeeded. retention can be configured with add-on retention packages; standard is 90 days but enterprise can get longer, and we can plug in to your SIEM via streaming.
[02:16] Priya Menon: is the KMS call trace stored in our project or in your control plane? regulatory preference is we store all key operation logs within our tenant in eu region.
[02:26] Jon Park: good question. currently key operation logs are emitted to the customer's logging bucket when CMK is used and where their KMS is the source of truth. when using redwood-managed keys, logs are in redwood control plane, but we can export. for EU-restricted tenants we recommend CMK so logs and key ops never leave the customer's region.
[02:45] Marco Ruiz: subprocessor list? we need names, locations, and whether they have access to cleartext.
[02:50] Leila O'Connell: we maintain a subprocessor register. high level: cloud infra providers in eu/us, metrics/telemetry vendor (redacted in this transcript), model hosting partners (some open-source models run on third-party GPU farms), and our support vendor. none of the subprocessors have access to plaintext unless it's part of a debug workflow and then it's tightly controlled and logged. we can share the full list in the next inbox update.
[03:19] Elias Novak: when you say model hosting partners, are you doing any cross-border batching or routing that could move tokens to the us?
[03:27] Jon Park: default routing is region-aware. we route requests to the nearest compatible region by policy. for strict region-pinning we can lock a tenant to eu-only endpoints and capacity. the only time we cross-border is on fallback when eu capacity is exhausted and customer policy allows for cross-border failover.
[03:45] Priya Menon: fallback is a no-go for us unless we have contractual permission. can you guarantee no cross-border routing, even in outages?
[03:53] Maya Thompson: yes, that's a common ask. we offer a hard-region lock config: if enabled, Redwood will not route requests out of the pinned region under any circumstances. tradeoff is degraded availability during zone/regional outages; we can offer dedicated capacity in eu with SLA to mitigate.
[04:12] Sara Lin: what about metadata and telemetry? sometimes headers or ip-level info leak. we need assurances that no identifying metadata crosses borders.
[04:20] Jon Park: we scrub or minimize metadata for pinned tenants; ip-based geolocation for metrics is aggregated and can be stored in-region. we can also provide an encrypted proxy to strip headers before ingestion. there are some telemetry tradeoffs but doable.
[04:36] Marco Ruiz: and encryption at rest/in transit — standard?
[04:40] Leila O'Connell: TLS 1.2+ in transit, AES-256 at rest. keys for rest encryption can be CMK in your KMS or redwood-managed HSM.
[04:50] Elias Novak: is there a split-KMS escrow SLA? who holds the other half?
[04:55] Jon Park: escrow typically put with an independent custodian; we have partnerships with two escrow providers who can hold shards under legal controls. we can also do a dual HSM setup where one shard remains in your HSM and the other in Redwood's HSM; the unlock requires both.
[05:12] Priya Menon: regarding subprocessor contracts — we need standard clauses: EU data transfer mechanisms, right to audit, breach notification timelines (48h), and proof of SOC 2/ISO for partners.
[05:25] Maya Thompson: absolutely; our DPA includes subprocessors and we can surface SOC 2 reports for main partners. we'll highlight breach notif timelines and audit rights.
[05:32] Elias Novak: ok can you sketch the flow: eu-customer sends request — everything stays in eu — which components are eu?
[05:40] Jon Park: sure. request hits eu ingress -> eu routing -> eu inference nodes (GPU cluster) -> if CMK mode, KMS in eu does decrypt of envelope key to perform decryption locally -> inference completes -> response encrypted and stored. logging is written to eu logging bucket. models themselves are either in eu model cache or pulled from eu model store. no control plane metadata leaves eu if tenant is pinned.
[06:06] Sara Lin: model updates — are model downloads pulled cross-region?
[06:09] Leila O'Connell: model artifacts are mirrored per region; for pinned tenants we ensure model artifacts are available locally. if a model variant isn't available in eu, we either replicate it (time window) or restrict to available models.
[06:23] Marco Ruiz: are there any third-party indices or embeddings stores that could leak vectors out of region?
[06:29] Jon Park: embedding indices for pinned tenants are stored in-region. shared caches are partitioned. we do not shard vectors across regions for pinned tenants.
[06:36] Priya Menon: one concern: law enforcement or governmental access. if there is a lawful request to redwood, what jurisdiction applies?
[06:44] Maya Thompson: good question. our control plane is in specific regions — lawful access requests are handled according to the jurisdiction controlling the data. for customer-managed keys and tenant pinned to eu, the keys and logs are under your KMS and in eu storage, so Redwood as a processor has limited ability to produce plaintext. we'll share our transparency report and process for handling lawful requests.
[07:06] Elias Novak: we need to understand the scenario where an eu customer accepts a us-subprocessor — do you do a DPIA?
[07:13] Leila O'Connell: we can support a DPIA — we have a template and can work with your privacy team to fill specifics.
[07:19] Marco Ruiz: can you explain the difference between soft region affinity vs hard pin? we have people using both terms internally.
[07:25] Jon Park: soft affinity: traffic is preferred to region A but can failover to region B when needed. hard pin: traffic must remain in region A; no failover. soft affinity usually gives better availability/cost; hard pin gives stronger residency guarantees.
[07:43] Sara Lin: from a cost perspective, what is the delta for hard pin + CMK + extended retention?
[07:49] Jon Park: general order of magnitude: hard pin with dedicated capacity in eu is the biggest driver (reserved GPU pools), CMK has minor overhead for KMS api calls, and extended log retention is add-on. for a rough estimate we will run a small sim. action item for jon to provide numbers.
[08:05] Priya Menon: audit logs format — can you provide a sample event? we want to automate ingest to our SIEM.
[08:11] Maya Thompson: yes we'll share a sample event schema and a syslog/streaming connector.
[08:15] Elias Novak: one more — does redwood ever do model evaluation or telemetry that requires seeing request payloads for performance tuning? we have strict rules about that.
[08:24] Leila O'Connell: only with explicit consent and opt-in. any performance tuning that needs payloads is done on anonymized or redacted data; for enterprise we can do in-region evaluation or have you run the eval harness on-prem.
[08:38] Marco Ruiz: about subprocessors again — want to ensure subcontractor chain is mapped down two levels. can we get that?
[08:45] Maya Thompson: yes we'll provide subprocessor mapping to two tiers and indicate which ones handle encrypted vs decrypted data.
[08:52] Priya Menon: can we talk about single-tenant vs multi-tenant isolation? are you offering tenant-isolated VMs or just logical partition?
[08:59] Jon Park: we offer both. hosted mode typically uses multi-tenant logical isolation with strong container/process boundary and network segmentation. dedicated/dedicated capacity can be single-tenant compute pools with tenant-only GPUs and network. for the highest assurance we recommend private deployment or dedicated pools.
[09:18] Sara Lin: do you support customer SSO provisioning for admin/RBAC? we want SCIM + SAML.
[09:23] Leila O'Connell: yes, SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for users and RBAC roles. we also support fine-grained route-level ACLs and audit trail of admin actions.
[09:35] Elias Novak: are admin actions logged with who changed config and before/after values?
[09:39] Jon Park: yes; configuration change events include actor, timestamp, target route/model, and diffs where available. those are exportable to your SIEM.
[09:47] Marco Ruiz: how do you prove compliance for subprocessors? do you collect partner SOC2 reports or do you rely on contractual attestations?
[09:54] Maya Thompson: both — we collect SOC 2/ISO attestations for core partners and contractual obligations for the rest. we maintain a vendor review cadence.
[10:02] Priya Menon: can you support a security questionnaire? we'll likely send an RfP security pack with 200+ ques.
[10:08] Maya Thompson: yes we do. we can return the completed package and prioritize questions around data residency and KMS.
[10:13] Elias Novak: how about encryption key rotation — who triggers rotations and what are expected downtimes?
[10:18] Jon Park: rotation is seamless for envelope keys; for CMK we call your KMS rotate API and update references; there should be no downtime if both sides honor key versioning. for shards/escrow it can require coordination but we can do rolling rotations.
[10:33] Sara Lin: are there test suites to validate that keys never leave region?
[10:36] Leila O'Connell: yes we have a test harness that runs synthetic requests and verifies route metadata, and we can provide audit artifacts from those tests.
[10:45] Priya Menon: curious about data at rest encryption for caches and kv-store. some vendors have been sloppy.
[10:50] Jon Park: our KV caches are encrypted at rest with either CMK or redwood HSM-managed keys; for pinned tenants those caches are provisioned in-region only.
[10:59] Marco Ruiz: support for KMS escrow with third-party custodian — any legal constraints?
[11:03] Maya Thompson: will need to be added to the DPA; custodian agreements and access controls are agreed upfront.
[11:09] Elias Novak: ok for timeline — if we want to pilot in q4, what do you need?
[11:15] Maya Thompson: SOC 2 docs + network diagram + list of tenant flows and which ones are EU-only. we will then size eu dedicated capacity and propose pricing.
[11:24] Leila O'Connell: i'd also schedule the security deep dive with priya to go through DPA and DPIA.
[11:29] Priya Menon: yes please, prefer week of 2026-09-28.
[11:33] Jon Park: i'll run the simulation after we get the traffic profile.
[11:36] Marco Ruiz: one operational question — who has emergency access to keys in Redwood-managed mode? is there a break-glass?
[11:42] Jon Park: there is a break-glass but it's logged, audited, and requires approval; for enterprise customers we can require a 2-person auth and provide notifications. we can also lock that down or remove break-glass if CMK is used.
[11:56] Maya Thompson: do you have any more questions?
[11:58] Elias Novak: no that's good for now. please send the SOC docs and subprocessor list.
[12:03] Maya Thompson: will do. quick recap of next steps — share SOC2 and ISO docs, sample audit log schema, subprocessor register, routing policy samples, and cost sim.
[12:13] Priya Menon: thanks everyone.
[12:15] End of transcript.
